ds-timeout-unknown-outcome.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed; pending independent review
ds-timeout-unknown-outcome.learning_objective: Describe partial failure and at-least-once delivery.

distractor_rationale.a: The work may have completed even though the response was not received.
distractor_rationale.b: The request may never have arrived.
distractor_rationale.d: Nothing guarantees the provider cancels anything.

follow_up_questions: How would you find out the real outcome of the charge?

ds-at-least-once-meaning.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed; pending independent review
ds-at-least-once-meaning.learning_objective: Describe partial failure and at-least-once delivery.

distractor_rationale.a: Ordering is a separate guarantee; the question asks what at-least-once implies.
distractor_rationale.b: At-least-once is specifically designed to prevent silent loss.
distractor_rationale.c: Integrity in transit is not part of a delivery guarantee.

follow_up_questions: Where would you store processed message ids so that the check and the work cannot disagree?

ds-read-your-writes.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed; pending independent review
ds-read-your-writes.learning_objective: Choose consistency guarantees for a feature.

distractor_rationale.a: Even synchronous replicas can briefly serve the old value unless remote_apply is used, and it adds latency and availability risk to every write.
distractor_rationale.c: A cache layered on the replica adds staleness rather than removing it.
distractor_rationale.d: Polling has no upper bound and adds load during lag spikes.

follow_up_questions: How could you implement the 'wait for the replica' approach using PostgreSQL's LSNs?

ds-dual-write-outbox.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed; pending independent review
ds-dual-write-outbox.learning_objective: Choose consistency guarantees for a feature.

distractor_rationale.a: Publishing first can announce orders whose commit then fails.
distractor_rationale.b: A retry cannot run if the process crashed between the calls.
distractor_rationale.d: Consumers are not participants in the producer's write; 2PC is also heavy and rarely supported.

follow_up_questions: How do consumers handle the duplicates the relay may produce?

ds-retry-amplification.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed; pending independent review

distractor_rationale.a: Miscounts the layers and keeps retries in two places.
distractor_rationale.d: The count is right, but more replicas feed the storm rather than stopping it.

follow_up_questions: Which layer would you keep retries in, and why?

ds-lww-clock-skew.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed; pending independent review

distractor_rationale.a: NTP narrows skew but cannot eliminate it, and the failure is silent.
distractor_rationale.c: Last-write-wins stores do not reject future timestamps by default.
distractor_rationale.d: Last-write-wins discards one write; it does not merge.

follow_up_questions: When is last-write-wins an acceptable choice despite this risk?

ds-idempotent-ordered-consumer.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed; pending independent review
follow_up_questions: How would you reprocess events after fixing a consumer bug?

ds-eventual-consistency.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
ds-eventual-consistency.learning_objective: Describe partial failure and at-least-once delivery.

distractor_rationale.a: That is linearizability or strong consistency.

follow_up_questions: Which user-facing feature would you not build on an eventually consistent store?

ds-circuit-breaker.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
ds-circuit-breaker.learning_objective: Choose consistency guarantees for a feature.

distractor_rationale.a: Multiplies load on a failing dependency.
distractor_rationale.d: More threads waiting on the same failure; the pile-up continues.

follow_up_questions: How would you choose the failure threshold and cool-down?

ds-kafka-partition-ordering.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review

distractor_rationale.a: Still unordered across partitions, and gives up parallelism.

follow_up_questions: What happens to per-key ordering if you later change the number of partitions?
